title: 2026 tax ratios, 2025 year-end results and Ombudsman report
subtitle: Also: accommodation tax agreements, grant equity across municipalities, capital underspending, vacant home tax and aggregate rates.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended keeping the 2026 property tax ratios unchanged and asked staff to prepare the by-laws for Regional Council on April 22. Staff said delay would push back tax bills from the area municipalities, so the committee moved ahead while asking for more information on vacant home taxes and aggregate rates {{vote:m4}}.

The committee also recommended approving preliminary 2025 financial results and amending the Surplus Allocation Policy {{vote:m3}}. Staff reported operating surpluses in tax-supported and water and wastewater programs, but only about half of the capital budget was spent. The committee accepted the Ombudsman's findings on closed meetings and directed staff to keep the transparency process begun in 2025 {{vote:m5}}. It also recommended delegating authority to sign Municipal Accommodation Tax agreements {{vote:m2}}.

The 2026 Grant Report was received for information. Councillors raised how grants are spread across the region's municipalities, and staff promised more data. The committee also heard that the grant policy will be reviewed by the next term of Council.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended keeping the 2026 property class tax ratios unchanged and directed staff to bring the by-laws to Regional Council on April 22, 2026 {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended receiving the 2025 Plan Update, approving the preliminary 2025 financial results, and amending the Surplus Allocation Policy {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended accepting the Ombudsman's findings and directing staff to maintain the 2025 process for transparency about closed-session reports {{vote:m5}}.

The committee recommended delegating authority to the CAO and Clerk to sign agreements with the area municipalities and the regional tourism marketing corporation for the Region's 10% share of the tax.

debate: On the grant report, one councillor argued that Cambridge organisations receive few grants and that advisory committees have little Cambridge representation. They asked for firmer geographic criteria. Others said many funded organisations serve the whole region wherever they are based.

Councillors asked why a one million dollar revenue threshold applies to key cultural institutions. Staff said it marks long-term durability and that organisations can move between categories. Staff said eligibility criteria will be reviewed next term.

On capital spending, a councillor said the Region treats other budget items as fixed but delivers only about half of planned capital. Staff cited supply chain delays, land acquisition timing and optimistic multi-year budgeting, and described an internal prioritization committee.

On tax ratios, councillors asked about aggregate rates and a vacant home tax. Staff said the aggregate rate was set under provincial rules and agreed to report back. Some councillors urged a quick vote because delay would raise later tax bills.
Councillors discussed property tax arrears and affordability. One said ratepayers cite several years of high Regional increases, and another noted police budget variances to follow up on.
